accepted.s:
With reference to resolutions in Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. A resolution is a self-contained proposal.
2. Every resolution is a substantive motion.
3. A mover may withdraw a resolution at any time without the leave of the House.
4. A resolution must be put to vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: A resolution is a self-contained proposal and always takes the form of a substantive motion. It must be put to vote, but its mover cannot withdraw it without the leave of the House.
accepted.tq: Test the procedural exception by identifying the statement that reverses the withdrawal rule.
accepted.sec: Resolutions - private member, government, statutory; AP equivalents

accepted.s: A resolution on the same subject as an earlier resolution is generally barred from being moved for what period?
accepted.x: A resolution on the same subject is barred for one year.
accepted.tq: Use the precise time-period distinction in procedural rules.
accepted.sec: Resolutions - private member, government, statutory; AP equivalents

accepted.s: Private Members’ Resolutions in Parliament are generally taken up on:
o: The last sitting day of every month
accepted.x: Private Members’ Resolutions are taken up on alternate Fridays during the afternoon.
accepted.tq: Match the device with its distinctive day-and-time arrangement.
accepted.sec: Resolutions - private member, government, statutory; AP equivalents

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a Government Resolution from a Private Members’ Resolution?
o: A Government Resolution is not a substantive motion, whereas a Private Members’ Resolution is a substantive motion.
A Government Resolution need not be put to vote, whereas a Private Members’ Resolution must be put to vote.
A Government Resolution is moved by a minister, whereas a Private Members’ Resolution is moved by a member who is not a minister.
A Government Resolution can be moved only in the Rajya Sabha, whereas a Private Members’ Resolution can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
accepted.x: A Government Resolution is moved by a minister. A resolution moved by a member who is not a minister is a Private Members’ Resolution; both are substantive motions and are put to vote.
accepted.tq: Separate the two similar devices by identifying who moves them.
accepted.sec: Resolutions - private member, government, statutory; AP equivalents

accepted.s: A resolution moved under a constitutional or statutory provision is known as a:
accepted.x: A resolution moved under a constitutional or statutory provision is called a Statutory Resolution.
accepted.tq: Match the procedural term with its legal basis.
accepted.sec: Resolutions - private member, government, statutory; AP equivalents

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding resolutions in the Andhra Pradesh Legislature is correct?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Legislature uses the same broad categories of parliamentary devices, including resolutions.
The Andhra Pradesh Legislature does not recognise resolutions used in Parliament.
Resolutions may be moved only during the Budget session in Andhra Pradesh.
Only statutory resolutions are available in the Andhra Pradesh Legislature.
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Legislature uses the same broad parliamentary devices, including private member, government and statutory resolutions.
accepted.tq: Apply the general parliamentary procedure to the State Legislature context.
accepted.sec: Resolutions - private member, government, statutory; AP equivalents

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an appropriate example of the subject of a Government Resolution?
o: A petition on a bill submitted by a citizen
A report of the Committee on Public Undertakings
Election of the Speaker by private members alone
accepted.x: A Government Resolution may be moved by a minister for purposes such as approving treaties.
accepted.tq: Identify the government-initiated matter from the nearby parliamentary devices.
accepted.sec: Resolutions - private member, government, statutory; AP equivalents

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Public Accounts Committee:
1. It consists of 22 members, comprising 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
2. Its members are elected annually by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.
3. A minister can be a member of the Committee.
4. Its Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Public Accounts Committee has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members, elected annually by proportional representation through the single transferable vote. Ministers cannot be members, and the Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker.
accepted.tq: Split the composition, election and eligibility statements before choosing the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s: Since 1967, the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee has generally been appointed from:
o: The ruling party in the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: Since 1967, the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee has been appointed from the Opposition.
accepted.tq: Remember the institutional convention rather than confusing it with the Estimates Committee convention.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s: The Public Accounts Committee, while examining expenditure, is particularly concerned with whether money was spent:
o: Only after approval by the Rajya Sabha
According to the policy of the Opposition
Within the scope of the demand
accepted.x: The Public Accounts Committee checks whether money was spent within the scope of the relevant demand and highlights waste, loss and nugatory expenditure.
accepted.tq: Focus on the precise audit-control expression rather than the broader idea of budget approval.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee?
o: They are binding on the executive in every case.
They can be implemented only after approval by the Finance Commission.
They are recommendations and are not binding on the executive.
They have the force of a judicial decree.
accepted.x: The recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee are not binding on the executive.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between legislative scrutiny and legally binding adjudication.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s: The Public Accounts Committee primarily examines the execution of financial decisions and does not ordinarily examine:
o: Expenditure within the scope of demands
accepted.x: The Public Accounts Committee examines execution and financial propriety, but it does not ordinarily examine the merits of government policy.
accepted.tq: Find the item outside the committee’s audit-and-execution mandate.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s: The present form of the Estimates Committee was established in 1950 on the recommendation of:
accepted.x: The present form of the Estimates Committee originated in 1950 on the recommendation of John Mathai.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the persons associated with different committees and reform areas.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s:
The Estimates Committee is correctly associated with which of the following functions?
1. Suggesting economies and administrative efficiency.
2. Suggesting alternative policies.
3. Examining the form of estimates.
4. Auditing CAG reports on public sector undertakings as its principal function.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Estimates Committee suggests economies, efficiency, administrative reforms, alternative policies and improvements in the form of estimates. Auditing CAG reports on public sector undertakings is associated with the Committee on Public Undertakings, not its principal function.
accepted.tq: Separate prospective examination of estimates from retrospective audit of public undertakings.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s: The Committee on Public Undertakings was created in 1964 on the recommendation of the:
accepted.x: The Committee on Public Undertakings was created in 1964 on the recommendation of the Krishna Menon Committee.
accepted.tq: Link the committee’s origin year with the correct recommending body.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Public Accounts Committee — ministers are eligible for membership
Committee on Public Undertakings — 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
Committee on Public Undertakings — examination of public sector undertakings and relevant CAG reports
Estimates Committee — Chairperson invariably from the Opposition
accepted.x: The Committee on Public Undertakings examines the reports and accounts of public sector undertakings and CAG reports relating to them. The other statements incorrectly interchange the features of the three financial committees.
accepted.tq: Use the committee-to-function match while rejecting swapped membership and chairperson features.
accepted.sec: Financial committees (PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings) - membership, chair, CAG reports

accepted.s: Which committee is described as the “Continuous economy committee”?
accepted.x: The Estimates Committee is known as the “Continuous economy committee.”
accepted.tq: Match the nickname with the committee concerned with economies and efficiency.
accepted.sec: Committee → nickname or role

accepted.s:
The term “watchdogs over the executive” is associated with which of the following groups of committees?
1. Public Accounts Committee
2. Estimates Committee
3. Committee on Public Undertakings
4. Department-related Standing Committees
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee, Committee on Public Undertakings, Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Committee on Government Assurances and Department-related Standing Committees are described as watchdogs over the executive.
accepted.tq: Recognise the inclusive option when all listed oversight committees perform executive scrutiny.
accepted.sec: Committee → nickname or role

accepted.s: Which committee tracks assurances and promises made by ministers until they are implemented?
o: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
accepted.x: The Committee on Government Assurances tracks assurances and promises made by ministers until implementation.
accepted.tq: Match the committee’s name with its specific monitoring role.
accepted.sec: Committee → nickname or role

accepted.s: The Committee on Papers Laid on the Table primarily checks whether:
o: The estimates contain alternative taxation policies
Public sector undertakings follow commercial principles
Papers laid by ministers, other than statutory orders, comply with the relevant requirements
accepted.x: The Committee on Papers Laid on the Table checks papers laid by ministers, other than statutory orders, for compliance.
accepted.tq: Distinguish documentary scrutiny from assurance-tracking and financial scrutiny.
accepted.sec: Committee → nickname or role

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is correct?
o: No minister can be a member of the Committee.
The Committee consists only of nominated members.
Only Rajya Sabha ministers are excluded from membership.
A minister may be a member if nominated by the Speaker.
accepted.x: No minister can be a member of the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Test the membership restriction directly, using the ministerial eligibility trap.
accepted.sec: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee or body)
a. Second Administrative Reforms Commission
b. Ashok Dalwai
c. Shanta Kumar
d. Nachiket Mor

List-II (Reform area)
i. Financial inclusion
 ii. FCI and PDS reform
 iii. Code of ethics, Right to Public Services and e-governance
 iv. Doubling farmers’ income

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Second ARC is associated with ethics, public services and e-governance; Ashok Dalwai with doubling farmers’ income; Shanta Kumar with FCI/PDS reform; and Nachiket Mor with financial inclusion.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped reform area.
accepted.sec: Committee oversight linked to reform areas

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kasturirangan — Education and the 5+3+3+4 structure
2. Urjit Patel — Inflation targeting at 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%
3. Nachiket Mor — Monetary policy framework
4. Shanta Kumar — Decentralised procurement and DBT for food
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kasturirangan is linked with education and the 5+3+3+4 structure, Urjit Patel with inflation targeting at 4% plus or minus 2%, and Shanta Kumar with FCI/PDS reform including decentralised procurement and DBT for food. Nachiket Mor is associated with financial inclusion, not monetary policy.
accepted.tq: Detect the deliberately swapped reform area in the third pair.
accepted.sec: Committee oversight linked to reform areas

accepted.s: The reform area associated with the Ashok Dalwai Committee includes:
o: DBT for food and decentralised procurement under the PDS
Value addition and land leasing in the context of doubling farmers’ income
Inflation targeting and monetary policy independence
accepted.x: Ashok Dalwai’s reform area concerns doubling farmers’ income, including value addition and land leasing.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy package that belongs to the specified reform objective.
accepted.sec: Committee oversight linked to reform areas

accepted.s: The Department-related Standing Committees (DRSCs) were introduced in:
accepted.x: The Department-related Standing Committees were set up in 1993.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the institutional introduction year from the origin years of financial committees.
accepted.sec: DRSCs, ad hoc, select and joint committees

accepted.s: How many Department-related Standing Committees are there, and how are they distributed between the two Houses?
o: 30: 20 under the Lok Sabha and 10 under the Rajya Sabha
22: 15 under the Lok Sabha and 7 under the Rajya Sabha
24: 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: There are 24 DRSCs: 16 are under the Lok Sabha and 8 are under the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Use the total-and-distribution combination rather than recalling only the total.
accepted.sec: DRSCs, ad hoc, select and joint committees

accepted.s: Each Department-related Standing Committee has:
o: 22 members, comprising 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha, with a quorum of 11
31 members, comprising 20 from the Lok Sabha and 11 from the Rajya Sabha, with a quorum of 12
31 members, comprising 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, with a quorum of 11
accepted.x: Each DRSC has 31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha. Its quorum is 11.
accepted.tq: Keep the committee’s total, House-wise composition and quorum together as separate numerical checks.
accepted.sec: DRSCs, ad hoc, select and joint committees

accepted.s: Who appoints the Chairpersons of Department-related Standing Committees?
o: The Prime Minister for Lok Sabha committees and the Vice-President for Rajya Sabha committees
The respective ministers heading the departments concerned
The Speaker for Lok Sabha committees and the Chairman for Rajya Sabha committees
accepted.x: The Speaker appoints the Chairpersons of Lok Sabha DRSCs, while the Chairman appoints the Chairpersons of Rajya Sabha DRSCs.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority-to-House distinction instead of attributing all appointments to one presiding officer.
accepted.sec: DRSCs, ad hoc, select and joint committees

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about ad hoc committees:
1. Inquiry committees may be set up by a motion or by the Speaker or Chairman.
2. A Committee on MPLADS is an example of an inquiry committee.
3. Ad hoc committees continue permanently after completing their assigned task.
4. Select and Joint Committees on Bills are included among ad hoc committees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Inquiry committees may be created by a motion or by the Speaker or Chairman; the Committee on MPLADS is an example. Select and Joint Committees on Bills are also ad hoc, and such committees end when their task is completed.
accepted.tq: Identify the false permanence statement and retain the statements describing formation and termination.
accepted.sec: DRSCs, ad hoc, select and joint committees

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a Select Committee from a Joint Committee on a Bill?
o: A Select Committee has members from one House, whereas a Joint Committee has members from both Houses.
A Select Committee is permanent, whereas a Joint Committee is temporary.
A Select Committee is appointed by the President, whereas a Joint Committee is appointed by the Speaker alone.
A Select Committee examines financial accounts, whereas a Joint Committee examines only petitions.
accepted.x: A Select Committee consists of members of one House. A Joint Committee consists of members of both Houses and is formed on a motion adopted in the House.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two bill committees by their House composition.
accepted.sec: DRSCs, ad hoc, select and joint committees

accepted.s: A Joint Committee on a Bill is formed through:
o: A motion adopted in the House
A resolution of the Finance Commission
An executive order issued by the Council of Ministers
A direction of the Comptroller and Auditor General
accepted.x: A Joint Committee on a Bill is formed on the basis of a motion adopted in the House.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct parliamentary mode of constitution rather than an executive or audit authority.
accepted.sec: DRSCs, ad hoc, select and joint committees

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of permanent Standing Committees?
o: Committee on MPLADS, Railway Convention Committee and Joint Committee on a Bill
Committee on MPLADS, Select Committee and Joint Committee on a Bill
Select Committee, Joint Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings
Business Advisory Committee, Committee on Petitions, Committee of Privileges and Committee on Rules
accepted.x: Business Advisory, Petitions, Privileges and Rules are examples of permanent Standing Committees. Inquiry committees and Select or Joint Committees on Bills are ad hoc and end after completing their tasks.
accepted.tq: Separate permanent standing bodies from task-specific ad hoc committees.
accepted.sec: DRSCs, ad hoc, select and joint committees
